subject: PoC trial plan & deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme-corp.com>, Pat Nguyen <pat.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC trial plan & deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Hi Alex / Pat —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we stay aligned on the PoC scope and the deployment mode decision (hosted API vs dedicated capacity vs private VPC/on-prem):

1) Goal / success criteria (what success looks like):
- 95th percentile latency under 300ms for 512-token conversational requests in production-like load (our perf target)
- Cost target: < $0.004 per inference at 10k qps-month equivalent (TBD by profiling)
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on your internal eval set (attached requirements matrix)
- Data controls: audit logs + per-route encryption requirements for PII flows

2) Deployment mode considerations you flagged:
- Hosted API: fastest to start, minimal ops, Redwood handles scaling; good if no strict VPC/KMS requirements.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool with capacity guarantees; good if you need predictable throughput and isolation but still want Redwood-managed infra.
- Private VPC / On-prem: required if you need customer-managed networking, HSM/KMS integration, or air-gapped environments. Longer lead time.

3) Suggested PoC plan (attached PDF):
- Week 0: Kickoff + account access and model selection (you indicated preference for open-model X-2.7q)
- Week 1: Integration: API keys, sample traffic, and baseline perf runs (hosted mode)
- Week 2: Dedicated capacity trial (if you want to test reserved throughput) — spin up a 1-node pool with profiling
- Week 3: Private/VPC feasibility (security checklist + network smoke test) — only if legal/Sec requires
- Week 4: Eval & handoff: compare latency, cost, and quality across modes; finalize recommendation

4) Stakeholders we identified on your side:
- Alex (product) — buyer & success criteria owner
- Pat (infra/security) — needs to sign off on VPC/HSM requirements
- Data Science / ML Engs — will validate quality with eval sets

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send the PoC plan and a short SOW draft (attached).
- Jordan (cc) will follow up with a short checklist of technical items we need for dedicated and private trials (network ports, KMS access, expected QPS).
- Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow whether you want us to run the initial baseline in Hosted API only, or include a Dedicated trial later in the PoC?

Thanks — appreciate the clarity so we can lock timelines.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan.pdf, acme_requirements_matrix.xlsx, sow-draft.docx

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC trial plan & deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. This lines up with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- We want to start with Hosted API for the baseline perf/quality runs to move fast. If numbers look promising, we’ll request a Dedicated trial to validate sustained throughput.
- Pat flagged the KMS/HSM requirement — for the PoC we can provide a customer-managed key for testing in the Dedicated slot, but Private VPC/on-prem will require legal sign-off and is likely out of scope for Q2.
- Timeline is tight for us this quarter; can we aim to finish the PoC by end of April?

Success criteria: same as you listed; I’ll attach our small eval set after this email.

Confirming: please kick off Hosted baseline and Jordan, please send the tech checklist.

Alex
Product Lead, Acme Corp
alex.rivera@acme-corp.com

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC trial plan & deployment mode follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Alex / Team —

Thanks — I’ll send the technical checklist shortly. Quick notes to set expectations for the Dedicated trial spin-up:

- Dedicated pool provisioning lead time: ~3 business days from signed trial SOW and capacity approval.
- For Dedicated we’ll need: CIDR ranges for VPC peering (if required), expected steady-state QPS, sample payload sizes, and any KMS endpoint for key wrapping tests.
- If you choose Dedicated for the PoC, we recommend a minimal 2-week dedicated trial so we can observe throughput and cold-start behavior under load.

Jordan

jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Folks —

Quick security notes from my side:
- For the baseline Hosted run, we need to ensure PII fields are redacted in transit; will share a redaction checklist.
- Dedicated trial: we can provide a customer-managed KMS (test key) and CIDR ranges.
- Private VPC/on-prem: will need a formal security review; not possible within the April timeline.

We’re comfortable starting with Hosted baseline as long as the Hosted endpoints support TLS 1.3 and we get the audit logs for the requests in the PoC window.

Pat

- Ben (me): send final PoC plan + SOW draft (attached). Will open HubSpot task and set tentative dates (kickoff Mon Apr 5).
- Alex: share eval set and confirm any additional success criteria by Mon Apr 4.
- Pat: share redaction checklist and the test KMS details if we move to Dedicated (Pat to confirm by Apr 4).

If there are no objections I’ll proceed with the plan and record the kickoff for Mon Apr 5.
